audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings may retain accelerated sale-leaseback cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.2 million filed cash proceeds; exact OE correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained sale proceeds inflate FY2025 OE and its negative $1.7 million anchor; omitted lease payments would also reduce projected OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The model sale-leaseback transaction generated homebuilding revenue of $ 45.0 million, home construction expense of $ 38.3 million, and cash proceeds of $ 36.2 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The sale-leaseback and $36.2 million proceeds are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show the OE calculation trace needed to prove how much was retained. The possible adjustment is material because the gross proceeds exceed the $24 million absolute base operating PV and equal about 36% of the $101 million base equity value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $36.2 million proceeds, $45.0 million revenue, $38.3 million expense, $8.8 million cash-flow adjustment and prepaid rent through FY2025 OE; remove retained monetization proceeds and rerun with recurring lease payments.

audit_findings.title: The valuation assumes all bridge cash is excess and distributable
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash and short-term investments directly to equity value without reserving operating liquidity.
audit_findings.evidence: While we believe we possess sufficient liquidity, we are mindful of potential short-term or seasonal requirements for enhanced liquidity that may arise to operate and grow our business.
audit_findings.explanation: The full cash add-back is demonstrated, although the amount actually required by operations remains unresolved. It is conclusion-determinative: $124.641 million exceeds every reported equity value of $98 million to $107 million, while the business used $375.674 million of operating cash during the latest nine months and had $340 million drawn on its revolver.
audit_findings.action: Establish minimum operating cash from seasonal construction needs, deposits, land commitments, covenant headroom, letters of credit and merger requirements; deduct that reserve from bridge cash and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 is not a sustainable after-tax earnings base
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.253 million of FY2025 tax credits; recurring cash impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The DCF grows the FY2025 OE anchor without an explicit normalization for higher cash taxes after new-home energy credits cease.
audit_findings.evidence: The OBBBA repeals many of the energy efficiency credits enacted under the Inflation Reduction Act, including our ability to claim energy efficient new home tax credits for homes that close after June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The statutory cutoff after June 30, 2026 is demonstrated, and FY2025 tax credits of $20.253 million are large relative to the negative $1.7 million anchor and $98 million to $107 million equity values. The precise valuation effect remains unresolved because the record does not trace cash taxes, deferred taxes or utilization of existing credit carryforwards.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2025 OE taxes, identify remaining usable credit carryforwards and their timing, calculate post-cutoff cash taxes, and rerun the DCF using normalized after-tax OE.

audit_findings.title: Development guarantees could consume cash ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $411.7 million gross instruments at June 30, 2026; incremental exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Calls, reimbursements or development spending not already captured in inventory reinvestment would reduce OE or the cash available in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We had outstanding letters of credit and surety bonds of $41.4 million and $321.9 million, respectively, as of September 30, 2025, primarily related to our obligations to local governments to construct roads and other improvements in various developments.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing reports $45.8 million of letters of credit, $361.3 million of surety bonds and $4.6 million of surety-backed letters of credit. These are not demonstrated losses, and the record does not establish which underlying costs are already included in inventory or forecast OE. Materiality therefore cannot be determined despite gross exposure far exceeding the reported equity values.
audit_findings.action: Map each instrument to its underlying project obligation, remaining recorded development cost and reimbursement terms; estimate probable calls and reserve only incremental cash requirements before rerunning the bridge and OE.

audit_findings.title: Pending litigation includes losses beyond recorded accruals that cannot be estimated
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.340 million recorded accrual; additional possible loss unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured or unindemnified settlements, judgments and defense costs would reduce future OE or cash in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, an estimate of possible loss or range of loss, if any, cannot presently be made with respect to certain of these pending matters.
audit_findings.explanation: A $12.340 million litigation accrual is already recorded at June 30, 2026, and the latest nine-month results include a litigation-related charge, so those recorded amounts are presently reflected in the filed numbers. The filing expressly states that additional losses for certain matters cannot be estimated; the existence and materiality of any unrecorded exposure therefore remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain matter-level asserted damages, procedural developments, insurance limits and exclusions, subcontractor indemnification and solvency, and management or counsel loss ranges; rerun OE and the bridge for any probable uninsured amount beyond the recorded accrual.
